text:
anna-platform: Opening a quota/limit request for new GPU canary pools in our sandbox VPCs (us-west-2). We need higher assignable public IP capacity and ENI headroom to avoid rollout throttles. Below is the ask and justification — please chime in if you want different numbers or a staged approach.

anna-platform: Requested increases (per account):
```
Account: 123456789012 (sandbox-gpu-usw2)
- Elastic IPs (EIP) quota: current 5 -> requested 120
- ENIs per VPC/subnet: current 30 -> requested 400
- Secondary private IPs per ENI: current 50 -> requested 200
- IPv6: enable /56 allocation + VPC IPv6 support
```

anna-platform: Why: we spin up GPU canary pools (NVIDIA A100 instances) across 3 AZs for early traffic testing. Each GPU node needs a public IP for model callbacks, health checks, and SIGTERM drain hooks during spot reclaims. We expect bursts during canary runs and need ENI/secondary IP capacity for node lifecycle + autoscaler churn. Staggered rollout planned: AZ-by-AZ, non-prod only initially.

raj: +1 on the ask, mostly agree. Can we split the request into two waves? E.g., 40 EIPs + 150 ENIs for wave 1, then the rest after verification. That should reduce risk of quota being rejected.

michelle: Question — can we avoid this by using internal NLB + NAT gateway? public EIPs are costly and limited. If we need public IPs for callbacks, can we route via a small egress fleet instead?

anna-platform: Good call. We evaluated NAT gateways but latency and client IP preservation for some services require public IPs. Also some partners validate origin IPs. For canaries we want minimal network hop to mimic production. We'll do wave1 smaller as @raj suggested.

tom: For clarity: ENI headroom requested per VPC (not per subnet) or per subnet? AWS quota is usually per AZ/subnet. We should request per-subnet ENI increases to avoid running into placement issues. Also list instance types: p4d and g5. Each instance uses 1 ENI + potential elastic network interfaces for multi-NIC setups.

anna-platform: Updated ask: per-subnet ENI quota -> request 130 ENIs per subnet across 3 subnets (AZs) for wave1 (total ~390), then bump to 400 per subnet for wave2 if approved. Including secondary IPs increase to support multiple pods per node.

cloud-ops: Opened AWS support case: Case ID 9876543210. Priority: high (we selected business-critical). ETA for initial response: ~24-48h. Linked ticket: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=9876543210

infra-bot: Created a tracking ticket in our internal tracker: INFRA-2641 and attached the cloud case.

michelle: Please add cost note in the case: per-EIP charges (when not in use) and extra ENI charges due to attached resources. Also mention compliance justification for public IPs.

anna-platform: Added cost/justification in the case: approx incremental cost estimate for wave1: ~120 EIPs allocated (but only ~40 in use) -> ~$200/month (rough), additional ENI/secondary IP usage nominal relative to instance costs. Wave2 cost scale projected ~3x.

raj: I'll own monitoring the AWS reply and the staging rollout. Action items: 1) split request into wave1/wave2 in cloud case, 2) tag all EIPs with cost-center=platform-canary, 3) update autoscaler to respect headroom.

tom: One more ask — can we request IPv6 allocation in the same case? IPv6 would reduce EIP needs long-term. If AWS supports enabling IPv6 per account quickly, that helps future-proof this.

cloud-ops: Included IPv6 enablement in the same case (asked for guidance on /56 allocation and whether VPC-level flags are needed). AWS support acknowledged and forwarded to network services team.

infra-bot: Reminder set: check case status in 48h and post updates here.

michelle: :thumbsup: Once we have wave1 approved, coordinate a small canary with infra engineer pair to validate NAT/timeouts/health-checks.

anna-platform: Thanks — waving this over to @raj for follow-up. I'll prepare the staged runbook and update INFRA-2641 with rollout steps and rollback plan.

raj: On it. I'll post a quick checklist in INFRA-2641 and ping here when AWS responds.

michelle: closing note — consider long-term network design doc to avoid repeating quota requests every major fleet onboarding. We should scope that after canary.

anna-platform: Agreed, added to backlog.
